A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have used dynamic-clamp to model Nav1.7 currents in DRG neurons and have demonstrated that the L858 mutation produces a dramatic increase in persistent current, resulting not only in a reduction in current threshold but also a 27-fold increase in sodium influx during sub-threshold depolarizations.

we have used the dynamic-clamp technique to show a direct link between the gain of function in the Nav1.7 L858H mutant and the hyperexcitability of nociceptors, which is likely to contribute to the pain phenotype of IEM.

the L858 mutation in Nav1.7 is sufficient to produce hyperexcitability in small DRG neurons and that the mechanism of this hyperexcitability is due to enhanced persistent sodium currents and enhanced net sodium influx during both subthreshold depolarization and interspike intervals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the L858I mutation produces a dramatic enhancement of persistent current that is likely to be responsible for the enhanced firing of action potentials observed in nociceptive neurons.
dynamic-clamp analysis of Nav1. 7 function in nociceptor neurons provides a mechanistic link to pain and that the IEM L858 mutation is a gain-of-function mutation.
dynamic-clamp is an effective tool for studying the function of Nav1.8 channels within nociceptive neurons.
